overview: Lean project on 12 wards in Hospitals A to D. After a 12-month baseline, all four hospitals map the catheter pathway in January 2027 and introduce standard work in February 2027, with monthly measurement to March 2028.
population: Adult inpatients on the 12 participating medical and surgical wards; all catheterised patients, including those catheterised in emergency or theatres before transfer.
exposure: Standard work: nurse-driven removal protocol, a daily catheter check at the morning huddle and a flowsheet removal reminder, introduced in all four hospitals at once.
procedures: Each hospital's champion leads a two-day mapping event with the Lean coach. Catheter days come from the nursing flowsheet in all four hospitals; indication documentation is checked on 20 charts per ward per month; infections follow the regional surveillance definition.

outcomes.name: Catheter days per 100 patient days
outcomes.measure: Monthly catheter days divided by patient days, per ward
outcomes.why: Responsive to removal practice and available from flowsheets.

outcomes.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections per 1,000 catheter days
outcomes.why: The harm patients care about; descriptive only.

outcomes.name: Catheters without a documented indication
outcomes.measure: Proportion of 20 sampled catheterised patients per ward per month

biasFlags.label: Secular trend
biasFlags.note: A simultaneous start cannot separate the project from regional trends.

biasFlags.label: Surveillance intensity
biasFlags.note: More attention to catheters may find more infections.

flags: One primary measure, one descriptive secondary
parsimony.simplestPath: Monthly catheter days per ward before and after one start date.

feasibility: One coach for three months per hospital; about 3 staff hours a month for point counts in Hospital D; chart review limited to 20 charts per ward per month for indication documentation.
theoreticalFramework: Lean value stream mapping and standard work; SEIPS only to describe the work system at handoffs.
summary: Simultaneous start in all four hospitals with flowsheet catheter days as the primary measure.
